title: fix(app-shell): see a predicate string arm nested one anyOf deeper
body:
Part of #9830 — deliverable one of the reshaped card. Deliverable two survives as a question that needs the declaration surface, so this does not close the card.

Implemented by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat, session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`.

## What was wrong

`SchemaForm`'s five name-convention detectors each gated on the same inline expression:

```
schema.type === 'string' || schema.anyOf.some(b => b.type === 'string')
```

That scan is ONE level deep. The platform serves a predicate that also accepts a boolean literal as a union inside a union, so the string arm is present and the scan returns false for it.

## The measurement — re-derived here, not inherited

Derived from the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 with `zod@4.4.3` through the same `z.toJSONSchema` call `/meta/types` is served with. The probe walks the derived document STRUCTURALLY — descending `properties`, `items`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `allOf`, resolving `$ref` against `$defs` — because the subject is a NESTING DEPTH, and any probe that flattens or stringifies the schema cannot see it.

SUBJECT — `action` `$.properties.visible`, authoring derivation, printed verbatim:

```json
{
  "description": "Visibility predicate — `true`/`false` literal, CEL string, or `{dialect, source}` envelope. The action is offered when it evaluates TRUE. Omit = always visible.",
  "anyOf": [
    { "type": "boolean" },
    {
      "anyOf": [
        { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
        {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "dialect": { "type": "string", "enum": ["cel", "cron", "template"] },
            "source": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
            "ast": {},
            "meta": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "rationale": { "type": "string" },
                "generatedBy": { "type": "string" }
              }
            }
          },
          "required": ["dialect"]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

one-level isString: **false** · predicate-named: **true** ⇒ no builder.

CONTROL — in the same command and the same derived document, `action` `$.properties.params.items.properties.visible`:

```json
{
  "description": "Param visibility predicate (CEL); omits the param when false.",
  "anyOf": [
    { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "dialect": { "type": "string", "enum": ["cel", "cron", "template"] },
        "source": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
        "ast": {},
        "meta": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "rationale": { "type": "string" },
            "generatedBy": { "type": "string" }
          }
        }
      },
      "required": ["dialect"]
    }
  ]
}
```

one-level isString: **true** ⇒ already routed. One product, one key name, two nesting depths, two faces.

Population, over the 30 metadata types the installed spec resolves a schema for:

| derivation | rows walked | predicate-named | pass one-level isString | rows where the nested-aware gate DISAGREES |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| output | 4059 | 67 | 2314 | **0** |
| authoring, IO-INPUT | 5170 | 110 | 3015 | **4** |

The four: `action.visible`, `action.disabled`, `object.actions[].visible`, `object.actions[].disabled`. `action` is one of the two types (with `view`) whose output derivation is degenerate, so it is the type served from the authoring retry arm. Per detector convention the disagreement is condition 4, field-ref 0, secret 0, icon 0, colour 0 — in BOTH derivations.

## The change

The gate is one named function, `admitsString`, that all five detectors call. It walks `anyOf` and `oneOf` together, because `pickBranch` and the scalar chain already read `schema.oneOf ?? schema.anyOf` as one union, and a detector that disagreed with the branch picker about what a union is would reopen the same split one combinator over. `allOf` is not walked: it is an intersection. It iterates with a visited set so a self-referential hand-written schema terminates.

Lifted out whole rather than patched in one detector, for the reason objectui#9859 gave in this same function: a fifth inline copy leaves the next detector holding the old scan. Measured to be a no-op for the other four today, which is what makes that safe rather than speculative.

## What it deliberately does NOT change

An empty schema is still not a string arm. The output-mode derivation emits an `anyOf` whose first arm is an empty schema for `hook.condition`, `sharing_rule.condition` and `field.visibleWhen` / `readonlyWhen` / `requiredWhen` — the transform on those keys erases its own input type. Verbatim, `hook` `$.properties.condition` in output mode:

```json
{
  "description": "Predicate (CEL); hook runs only when TRUE.",
  "anyOf": [
    {},
    {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "dialect": { "type": "string", "enum": ["cel", "cron", "template"] },
        "source": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
        "ast": {},
        "meta": { "type": "object", "properties": { "rationale": { "type": "string" }, "generatedBy": { "type": "string" } }, "additionalProperties": false }
      },
      "required": ["dialect"],
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  ]
}
```

JSON Schema says an empty schema admits everything, strings included. It is equally what "we could not derive this" looks like on the wire. Reading it as a string arm would mount a CEL builder on any predicate-named key that derived to nothing, including a genuinely boolean-only one.

## Deliverable two — the answer, and the half that needs the declaration surface

The precedence is three-tier and was already implemented, just not written down anywhere: an explicit `fieldSpec.widget` wins outright (`resolveFieldWidget` runs no detector at all when the form spec pinned one); then the SHAPE test vetoes; then the NAME convention selects among the widgets whose shape fits. Neither side wins globally. That is now written into `admitsString`'s own header, on objectui's side, because it is a description of what this engine does.

The half that does not settle here: when the served shape is uninformative — the erased husk above — does the name convention get to override it? Answering that needs a signal only the declaration side can send: the server serving the authoring derivation (which objectstack's own `toJsonSchemaSafe` header records as proposed, measured and refused), a form spec pinning the widget, or a marker on the envelope this engine could recognise. This PR does not adjudicate it, and the seat is asked to route that half back to triage.

## Pin and ablations

`SchemaForm.nestedAnyOfPredicate-9830.test.tsx`, co-located with the component's other pins, drives the real `SchemaForm` and reads the rendered face, scoped per field by the host label id. One render carries four properties: the nested predicate (subject), the flat predicate (control that was green before), the erased husk (boundary), and a plain non-predicate string (negative control).

Ablation 1 — revert `admitsString` to the one-level scan. Anchor hit once; blob `939227f5a6e5` to `7828401f49b0`. Result 3 failed / 2 passed: the nested case red, and the accounting case red reading `['condition']` instead of `['visible', 'condition']` — so the flat control still fired under the old code, which is the disagreement this card is about. Restored: blob equals HEAD `939227f5a6e5` and `git diff HEAD` empty.

Ablation 2 — widen the gate the other way, reading an empty schema as a string arm. Anchor hit once; blob `939227f5a6e5` to `bba9cb6d0630`. Result 2 failed / 3 passed: the husk boundary red, accounting red reading `['visible', 'condition', 'hidden']`, while subject and control stayed green. Restored, same proof. So the boundary assertion is not vacuous either.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts` — 274 files, 2899 passed, 1 skipped
- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/components/` — 25 files, 361 passed
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` — clean, after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` (a fresh worktree reports TS2307 until the closure exists; that is a prerequisite, not a gate)
- `eslint` on both changed files — exit 0, 16 pre-existing warnings, none on a changed line
- gates, all exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the three changed paths — NOT GOVERNED

The narrowing: `admitsString` is module-private, and its only observable effect is which widget the five detectors resolve, reachable only through `resolveFieldWidget`, which has exactly two callers, both inside `SchemaForm.tsx`. The affected population is therefore every test that renders `SchemaForm` — enumerated by import rather than by identifier — which is the metadata-admin tree plus console's `FormPage`. The full `packages/app-shell` tree is left to CI.

## Pending-changeset sweep

`check:changeset-claims` reports three pending changesets naming `SchemaForm.tsx`; each was read, and none is made false by this diff.

- `6247-option-visiblewhen-metadata-admin.md` — front matter `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` — about per-option predicate filtering; this diff touches no option filtering.
- `console-form-container-specs-one-declaration-5596.md` — front matter `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` and `'@object-ui/console': patch` — about the section and view spec declarations; untouched here.
- `formfieldspec-dependson-5040.md` — front matter `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` — its claim that `SchemaForm.tsx` re-exports `FormFieldSpec` and `VisibilityPredicate` still holds.
